title: Uniform cohomological ranges for geometric duality and nearby cycles
statement:
Fix $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$ and $\ell\ne p$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Over any separably closed field $F$ of characteristic $p$, and for every separated finite-type $F$-scheme $Z$, put $\omega_Z=Ra_Z^!A$ and $D_Z=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_Z)$, using the etale constructible exceptional operation and tensor--Hom adjunction as in [def-trf-dualizing-complex]. These formulas extend to bounded constructible complexes without a finite-Tor condition, and $D_Z$ takes such complexes to bounded constructible complexes. There is an integer $c_d$, depending only on a dimension bound $d$, such that $D_Z(D_c^{\leq0})\subset D^{\geq c_d}$ whenever $\dim Z\leq d$.

Let $B$ be an excellent strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] equal-characteristic-$p$ trait with algebraically closed residue field, and $X\to B$ separated of finite type, of dimension at most $d$. Let $R\Psi_X=i^*R\bar j_*$ on small etale sites, where $i:X_0\to X$, $\bar j:X_{\bar\eta}\to X$. Then $R\Psi_X$ has finite cohomological dimension bounded in terms of $d$, preserves bounded constructibility, and both exact contravariant functors
$$F_X=R\Psi_X D_{X_{\bar\eta}},\qquad G_X=D_{X_0}R\Psi_X$$
send $D_c^{\leq0}(X_{\bar\eta},A)$ into $D^{\geq b_d}$ for some integer $b_d$ independent of $X$ and of finite trait extensions. Their extensions to $D^-_c$ have the same lower bounds. The bounds for $F_X,G_X$ can also be chosen as functions of $\dim X_{\bar\eta}$ alone, independently of vertical components of $X$. The corresponding two functors $q^*D_Z$ and $D_{Z_K}q^*$ for a separably closed extension $K$ of an algebraically closed field $F$ also have uniform lower bounds depending only on $d$. All functors here are exact on their derived models. No assertion about an isomorphism between $F_X$ and $G_X$ is made.

Excellence of a scheme means excellence of its affine coordinate rings [def-exc-excellent-ring].

proof.text: Work in the ordinary etale derived categories. A separated finite-type scheme over any field is Noetherian and its structure map admits a Nagata compactification. The ambient exceptional-adjoint theorem therefore supplies $a_Z^\times$ with no constructible or finite-Tor restriction. Define $\omega_Z=a_Z^\times A$ and $D_ZM=R\mathcal Hom_A(M,\omega_Z)$. This is the etale reading of the formulas in the statement. We do not apply a theorem restricted to the fixed algebraic closure of a finite field.

proof.text:
Suppose $\dim Z\leq d$. For an affine etale finite-type neighbourhood $u:U\to Z$, etale local dimension gives $\dim U\leq d$. Such $u$ is separated (both schemes are separated over the field) and $a_U$ is compactifiable. Ambient etale adjoint locality gives $u^*\omega_Z=a_U^\times A$. Thus
$$\operatorname{Hom}(A_U,u^*\omega_Z[q])=\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_{U!}A_U,A[q]).$$
Compact-support amplitude puts $Ra_{U!}A_U$ in $D^{[0,2d]}$. On the separably closed point, every affine etale object is a finite disjoint union of the point by the split-etale-algebra statement. The sheaf axiom therefore identifies its module sheaves with ordinary modules (values on those unions are finite products). The coefficient ring $A$ is self-injective, so the right side vanishes for $q<-2d$: coefficient Hom reverses degrees and has no higher Ext. These Hom groups compute the degree-$q$ cohomology of sections of a K-injective representative restricted to $U$. Their presheaf sheafifies to $\mathcal H^q(\omega_Z)$: kernels of a complex of sheaves are computed sectionwise and its cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels. Hence $\omega_Z\in D^{\geq-2d}$. This proves the quantitative bound over the actual separably closed field, uniformly in $n$.

proof.text:
The finite-coefficient adjoint comparison is stated over an arbitrary positive-characteristic field. Apply it to $a_Z$ and the constant free rank-one object $A$ on the point, which is bounded constructible with Tor amplitude $[0,0]$. It states that $
u_Z^*a_Z^	imes R
u_{s,*}A$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Site comparison identifies $R
u_{s,*}A$ with the ordinary constant $A$. By the preceding lower bound $\omega_Z$ is in $D^+$, so the site-comparison unit applies. The finite-ring constructible-origin theorem then implies that $\omega_Z$ itself is bounded constructible. Only the coefficient object at the point has been assumed finite-Tor here, not the argument $M$ of $D_Z$.

proof.text:
Let $M\in D^{\leq b}(Z,A)$ and put $c=-2d$. For every etale object $U$, restriction is exact, so $M|_U\in D^{\leq b}$ and $\omega_Z|_U\in D^{\geq c}$. If $t<c-b$, standard t-structure orthogonality gives $\operatorname{Hom}(M|_U,\omega_Z|_U[t])=0$, since $c-t>b$. The local K-injective Hom computation identifies this with the degree-$t$ cohomology of the presheaf Hom complex on $U$. Sheafifying, as in Step 2, gives $\mathcal H^t(D_ZM)=0$. Consequently
$$D_Z(D^{\leq b})\subseteq D^{\geq-2d-b}.$$
This argument applies on the whole unbounded derived category, in particular to $D^-_c$, without a finite-Tor or constructibility assumption on $M$.

proof.text:
First prove constructible preservation for residue-field coefficients $k_E=A_{E,1}$. The preceding step makes the ordinary etale dual of a bounded $M$ bounded below. Pull $M$ and $\omega_Z$ to the pro-etale site. The finite-field internal-Hom finiteness theorem applies over any field, hence its Hom is bounded constructible and has a bounded constructible etale origin $Q$. Identify $Q$ with the ordinary etale Hom as follows. For every bounded-below etale test complex $C$, site comparison, monoidality, and tensor--Hom adjunction identify
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C,Q)=\operatorname{Hom}(
u^*C,R\mathcal Hom(
u^*M,
u^*\omega_Z))=\operatorname{Hom}(C\otimes^L M,\omega_Z).$$
All full-faithfulness uses are in $D^+$: over the field $k_E$, tensor with bounded $M$ preserves bounded-below objects. Yoneda on $D^+$ identifies $Q$ with $D_ZM$. This proves bounded constructibility for $n=1$ without identifying the ground field with the fixed finite-field closure.

proof.text: For the fixed $A=A_{E,n}$, a constructible sheaf $M$ has the finite filtration $M\supseteq\varpi M\supseteq\cdots\supseteq\varpi^nM=0$. Its subquotients $M_j=\varpi^jM/\varpi^{j+1}M$ are constructible sheaves of $k_E$-modules, by constructible Serre closure; no flatness is asserted. The coefficient-dual restriction lemma identifies $D_{Z,A}(\operatorname{Res}M_j)$ with $\operatorname{Res}D_{Z,k_E}M_j$, bounded constructible by the preceding step; restriction of coefficients retains the finite locally constant stratification. Starting at $\varpi^nM=0$, apply the contravariant exact Hom functor to each short exact filtration triangle. Its cohomology long exact sequence and Serre closure prove bounded constructibility for $D_{Z,A}M$ by descending finite induction on $j$. Finally build any bounded constructible complex from its finitely many cohomology sheaves by the truncation triangles and apply the same argument. This proves the whole constructibility clause for all $n$; the bound $c_d=-2d$ was proved independently in Step 4.

proof.text:
Put $r=\dim X_{\bar\eta}$ when the generic fibre is nonempty. The map $\bar j$ is affine, hence qcqs: it is the generic open immersion followed by an algebraic field extension. For every geometric point $x$ of $X_0$, the strict-local stalk formula and exactness of $i^*$ give
$$(R^q\Psi M)_x=H^q(X_{(x)}\times_B\bar\eta,M)=\varinjlim_U H^q(U_{\bar\eta},M|_{U_{\bar\eta}}).$$
Here $U$ ranges over a small cofinal system of affine pointed etale neighbourhoods of $x$ with affine transitions; continuity applies with base $X_{\bar\eta}$ and the sheaf $M$ in degree zero. Each $U_{\bar\eta}$ is finite type over the separably closed generic field and has dimension at most $r$, by etale local dimension. The relative torsion dimension bound gives vanishing for $q>2r$ for every module sheaf $M$, without constructibility. The module/abelian comparison permits this computation after forgetting the coefficient action. Conservativity of stalks gives $R^q\Psi M=0$ for $q>2r$.

proof.text: The finite bound just proved is on all sheaves. It gives $\Psi(D^{\leq b})\subseteq D^{\leq b+2r}$ even for unbounded inputs, as follows. Write $T=i^*\bar j_*$ and $N=2r$. Its total derived functor is $i^*R\bar j_*$, since $i^*$ is exact. For $K\in D^{\leq b}$ choose a K-injective representative $I$ with injective terms. Above degree $b$ it is exact. The sequences $0\to Z^tI\to I^t\to Z^{t+1}I\to0$ for $t\geq b$ give $R^qT(Z^{b+N}I)=R^{q+N}T(Z^bI)=0$ for $q>0$. Thus the good truncation $\tau^{\leq b+N}I$, still representing $K$, has $T$-acyclic terms. The finite-cd acyclic-complex theorem computes $RTK$ by applying $T$ to this truncation, which is zero above $b+N$. On a bounded-below input the injective resolution starts at its lower bound, giving $\Psi(D^{\geq a})\subseteq D^{\geq a}$. No infinite truncation induction or convergence assertion is needed.

proof.text: For nearby-cycle constructibility it suffices to treat a constructible sheaf on the geometric generic fibre. One may use a separable closure $K^s$ of $K=\operatorname{Frac}B$. If an algebraic closure $\bar K$ was chosen, its extension over $K^s$ is purely inseparable, and the projection $X_{\bar K}\to X_{K^s}$ is a universal homeomorphism by the inseparable-closure invariance statement (applied to the $K^s$-scheme $X_{K^s}$); topological invariance identifies the etale module categories and direct images. It preserves constructibility: carry a finite locally closed stratification through the universal homeomorphism, use reduced structures on the strata, and descend their finite locally constant restrictions through the etale-site equivalence. Let $M$ now be on $X_{K^s}$. The finite separable subextensions $L/K$ form a small directed system, with affine transition maps and limit $X_{K^s}$ (on affines tensoring commutes with the union of the fields). Constructible-module limit descent supplies a finite separable $L/K$ and a constructible $M'$ on $X_L$ pulling back to $M$.

proof.text: For $v:X_L\to X_K$, finite separability makes $v$ finite etale. It is finitely presented since $X_K$ is Noetherian. The finite pushforward theorem gives the constructible sheaf $H=v_*M'$ and $Rv_*M'=H$. Over $K^s$, proper base change identifies $H|_{X_{K^s}}$ with the pushforward along $w:X_L\times_KK^s\to X_{K^s}$ of the pullback of $M'$. The chosen embedding $L\subset K^s$ supplies a section of $w$; a section of a separated etale map is open and closed. The section component and its complement split this pushforward as a product, whose first factor is $M$. Restriction to that factor and extension by zero give $M\xrightarrow{u}H|_{X_{K^s}}\xrightarrow{v_0}M$ with $v_0u=1$. This splitting does not divide by $[L:K]$.

proof.text: Apply sheaf nearby-cycle finiteness to $H$ on the arithmetic generic fibre. Its trait is the actual strictly henselian DVR $B$, its residue field is separably closed, $X$ is separated finite type, and the finite coefficient exponent is invertible; no model trait $k[t]_{(t)}$ is substituted. Each $R^q\Psi(H|_{X_{K^s}})$ is constructible. Apply the additive functor $R^q\Psi$ to the splitting in Step 10. Its first factor is the kernel of $1-R^q\Psi(u v_0)$ and is constructible by Serre closure. Thus every $R^q\Psi M$ is constructible, and Step 7 supplies the uniform vanishing above $2r$. A finite induction through truncation triangles proves bounded constructibility for every bounded constructible input.

source.place: Illusie, Grothendieck and vanishing cycles (2021), §§1.1--1.2, printed pp. 85--86, formula (1.2) and final constructibility paragraph; geometric-sheaf extension by the explicit splitting in Steps 9--10.

proof.text: Let $W$ be the scheme-theoretic closure of $X_\eta$ in $X$. On an affine chart with ring $C$ its ring is $C/\ker(C\to C[1/t])$, where $t$ is a uniformizer of the DVR of $B$. Multiplication by $t$ is injective on this quotient: if $tc$ is killed by a power of $t$, then so is $c$. Every nonzero base element is a unit times a power of $t$, so this quotient is torsion free over the DVR. The PID torsion-free flatness theorem makes $W\to B$ flat. The closure is closed in the Noetherian $X$, hence finite type. Apply the flat-family generic-dimension node with base the integral trait $B$ to obtain $\dim W_0\leq\dim W_\eta=r$. Equality of generic and geometric generic dimensions follows from field-extension dimension invariance. This is the dimension argument that excludes arbitrarily large vertical components.

proof.text:
Let $h:W\hookrightarrow X$ and $h_0:W_0\hookrightarrow X_0$. The generic base change $h_{\bar\eta}$ is an isomorphism. Direct-image composition gives $R\bar j_{X*}L=Rh_*R\bar j_{W*}L$. Proper base change for $h$ along $X_0\to X$, valid on unbounded torsion-module complexes, now identifies
$$R\Psi_X L\simeq Rh_{0*}R\Psi_W L.$$
The open--closed recollement statement includes exactness of closed pushforward on etale module sheaves, so $Rh_{0*}=h_{0*}$ preserves each cohomological bound. This proves the support comparison for all the inputs under consideration.

proof.text:
On the special fibre, the closed ambient adjunction gives $Rh_{0*}\dashv Rh_0^!$. Compact-support composition identifies $Ra_{X_0!}Rh_{0*}$ with $Ra_{W_0!}$, since the closed immersion is proper. The composition-of-right-adjoints lemma gives $Rh_0^!\omega_{X_0}=\omega_{W_0}$. Apply the ambient immersion-Hom identity to $s=h_0$ and second argument $\omega_{X_0}$; it is valid without boundedness or finite Tor hypotheses. It yields
$$D_{X_0}(h_{0*}M)\simeq h_{0*}D_{W_0}M.$$
All structural maps here are over the algebraically closed residue field.

proof.text: For $L\in D_c^{\leq0}(X_{\bar\eta},A)$, Step 4 gives $D_{X_{\bar\eta}}L\in D^{\geq-2r}$, and the lower exactness bound of Step 8 gives $F_XL\in D^{\geq-2r}$. Also Step 8 gives $R\Psi_WL\in D^{\leq2r}$; apply Step 4 on $W_0$, whose dimension is at most $r$ by Step 12, to get $D_{W_0}R\Psi_WL\in D^{\geq-4r}$. Steps 13--14 give $G_XL\in D^{\geq-4r}$. Thus $b_r=-4r$ works for both functors. Exactly the same calculation works on $D^-_c$, since Steps 4, 8, 13 and 14 were established on the required unbounded derived categories. If $X_{\bar\eta}$ is empty, its input category is zero and both functors vanish. If $\dim X\leq d$, then $r\leq d$, so $b_d=-4d$ works as well. Repeating the argument over any finite extension of the trait uses the same $r$, by field-extension dimension invariance. No bound on vertical components enters.

proof.text: Finally $q^*$ is exact for constant coefficients and preserves constructibility; field extension preserves $\dim Z$. Hence $q^*D_Z$ carries $D_c^{\leq0}$ into $D^{\geq-2d}$ by Step 4 over $F$, and $D_{Z_K}q^*$ does so by Step 4 over the actual separably closed $K$. The calculation applies to $D^-_c$ as well. Derived internal Hom is exact contravariantly, derived direct image is triangulated, and the exact inverse images induce exact derived functors. Their composites are therefore exact on the derived models in the statement.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q77-41c2b5d2a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, all 16 steps, both new nodes, all 62 cited statements, unit sk-i-curve-zero and Stacks 0H3X (more-morphisms.tex l.5256). The item statement is unchanged and not weakened. Every step checks out. The bound omega_Z>=-2d comes from adjoint locality, compact-support amplitude [0,2d] and self-injectivity of A. That gives D_Z(D^{<=b})>=-2d-b on the unbounded category. Constructibility of omega comes from lem-pur G_A(A), the finite-ring etale origin and D^+ full faithfulness. The k_E case is Bhatt-Scholze finiteness plus a Yoneda argument entirely in D^+. The case of general n uses the uniformizer filtration and the new coinduction lemma. Nearby-cycle cohomological dimension 2r comes from the strict-local stalk limit and the relative torsion dimension bound. The unbounded upper bound follows from a T-acyclic good truncation. Constructibility goes through a finite separable descent and a direct-summand argument. For G_X: the horizontal closure W is flat, so dim W_0<=r, and the support and closed-pushforward identities give the common bound -4r. Both new nodes are true and are not duplicates or restated clauses. The flat-family node is Stacks 0H3X with F=O_Y. I proved the coinduction lemma myself: Res commutes with Ra_!, right adjoints compose, and Hom_A(k_E,A)=ann(varpi)=k_E.
